name: Trebol/monolith-to-microservices
description: Decomposes the Trebol eCommerce Spring Boot monolith (org.trebolecommerce:trebol-backend-monolith-java17) into three independently deployable services — Identity, Catalogue and Orders — consuming the business-rules-extraction manifest as input. Enforces four mandatory prerequisite gates inside the monolith before any extraction: replace cross-domain repository reads with contracts, publish the 54-code authority catalogue as a generated artefact, and record the consistency and authentication-propagation decisions. Carries a 17-item defect decision register, seven items of which must be fixed before extraction. REPOSITORY-SPECIFIC: names concrete classes, authority codes and order statuses from this codebase; not applicable to any other repository.

matchingCriteria._comment: Primary: the exact Maven coordinates of this repository.
Secondary: the prerequisite analysis output must already be present, since this transformation consumes it rather than producing it.

transformations.name: AWS/business-rules-extraction
transformations.reason: This transformation consumes the Mode A domain manifest, global schema, seed data, coupling hotspots, integrations map and authentication model it produces. Without them the pre-flight validation in SKILL.md fails.

knownGaps: Porting-depth specifications exist for the person and image domains only. The remaining ten are covered at Mode A depth, which is sufficient for planning but not for porting; each phase therefore begins by producing them for the domains it touches.
The order and billing domains have no porting-depth specification yet, and order is the largest and most complex domain in the system (58 files, 4243 LOC, 70 rules).
No event infrastructure exists anywhere in the codebase — no broker, queue or stream — so the outbox required by defect D11 is built from nothing.
